candidates.description: At the beginning of pursuing a goal, people are more committed to a moderate, proximal goal than to an ambitious, distal goal.
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study is a close replication of Heath et al. (1999)'s with two main objectives.
candidates.notes: The proximal-goal option was not the most frequently selected; equal commitment was selected more often.

candidates.description: People perceive more progress toward a moderate, proximal goal than toward an ambitious, distal goal.
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study is a close replication of Heath et al. (1999)'s with two main objectives.

candidates.description: At the end of pursuing a goal, people are more committed to a moderate, proximal goal than to an ambitious, distal goal.
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study is a close replication of Heath et al. (1999)'s with two main objectives.

candidates.description: Smaller and more proximal subgoals increase the likelihood of achieving the overall goal.
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study is a close replication of Heath et al. (1999)'s with two main objectives.

candidates.description: In the absence of a specific goal, people prefer a lower-risk option over a higher-risk option involving gains.
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study is a close replication of Heath et al. (1999)'s with two main objectives.

candidates.description: When falling behind a specific goal, people are more willing to choose a higher-risk option than when no specific goal is present.
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study is a close replication of Heath et al. (1999)'s with two main objectives.
candidates.notes: Both conditions showed a preference for the lower-risk option, but the authors interpret the relatively greater preference for the higher-risk option when below a goal as support for the original hypothesis.
